prompt: Complete DigitRunReader.readNumbers so it scans a byte stream with a PushbackInputStream, collecting digit runs as numbers and treating a '-' as a sign only when the next byte is a digit.
explanation: Plain streams are read-forward only, so a scanner that has to look one byte ahead needs somewhere to put that byte back; PushbackInputStream.unread does exactly that, and the next read returns it again. Both places here need it: after a digit run you have already consumed the terminating byte, and after a '-' you have consumed the byte that decides whether it was a sign. Building the value as value * 10 + (c - '0') turns the ASCII codes into a number without allocating a String.
hints: read() gives you an int: -1 for end of stream, otherwise the byte value, so c >= '0' && c <= '9' tests for a digit.
Write a small helper that consumes a whole digit run, given the first digit, and unreads the byte that ended it.
Never unread -1 -- check for end of stream before calling unread.
